Laboratories must comply with the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988. Congress passed CLIA in 1988 establishing quality standards for all laboratory testing performed on clinical samples to ensure the accuracy, reliability and timeliness of patient test results regardless of where the test was performed. CLIA requires all entities that perform even one test, including waived tests on "materials derived from the human body for the purpose of providing information for the diagnosis, prevention or treatment of any disease or impairment of, or the assessment of the health of, human beings" to meet certain federal requirements. If an entity performs tests for these purposes, it is a laboratory under CLIA, and the entity must register with the CLIA program.

Laboratories are not state licensed. The Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services directs state health agencies or other appropriate agencies to determine if health care entities meet federal standards. This helping function is called "CLIA certification".
Health Facility Compliance Unit staff are responsible for inspecting laboratories for CMS. For more information on the certification process, contact your regional office (PDF) .

After March 1, 2026, paper fee coupons and CLIA certificates will no longer be available. Laboratories must switch to email notifications to start receiving electronic CLIA fee coupons and certificates.
To switch to electronic notifications or update an email address, a laboratory must:
Provide notification to your regional CLIA office by email; or
Fill out the CMS-116 application (PDF) . (Note: To switch to electronic notifications, check the box, "Receive notifications including electronic certificates via email.")

Laboratories must make sure CMS has their most up-to-date email address on file to receive important CLIA updates and information. HHSC CLIA recommends using a business email address, or one that many staffers can access and use.

Laboratories may be accredited. Accrediting programs are: Joint Commission for the Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations; American Osteopathic Association; American Association of Blood Banks; College of American Pathologists; Commission on Office Laboratory Accreditation and American Society of Histocompatibility and Immunogenetics.
For certification, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) uses the CMS-116 Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Application for Certification (PDF) .
On behalf of the CMS CLIA program, HHSC uses Form 3225, Application for Certification – Supplement to CMS 116 to process CLIA certificate applications.

All initial CLIA applications for laboratories located in Texas are processed by HHSC CLIA regional offices. Applications for all certificates, except Certificates of Waiver, must include Lab Director qualifications documentation. Laboratories must complete the CMS-116 application entirely. HHSC CLIA will not process incomplete applications. For questions about the status of a CLIA application, the laboratory should contact their CLIA regional office.

All laboratories must notify HHSC CLIA within 30 days of any change to the facility name, location, contact information or ownership. All laboratories, except those with a Certificate of Accreditation, must notify HHSC CLIA within 30 days of any change to the Laboratory Director. Laboratories can make a change notification by submitting the CMS-116 or sending a letter to HHSC CLIA.

A new CMS-116 form is required to add a multiple site exception or make changes to the certificate type, ownership or nonwaived Laboratory Director. Laboratories must fill out the form in its entirety, regardless of whether any other information is changing. Laboratories must include Lab Director qualifications documentation for a change to Laboratory Director. Laboratories with a Certificate of Waiver do not need to provide any extra documentation and may request a Director change by sending a letter to HHSC CLIA.

Laboratories requesting changes to existing multiple sites, facility name, tax ID, location, contact information, Technical Supervisor or waived Laboratory Director, must send a letter to HHSC CLIA which includes:
Signature of the Laboratory Director or designee
For more information on fee amounts, visit the CMS CLIA Certificate Fee Schedule (PDF) .

All laboratories can pay their CLIA certification fee online through a secure platform hosted by the U.S. Treasury Department. To make a payment online, CMS utilizes Pay.gov . Laboratories must submit all CLIA fees directly to CMS through their payment website, Pay.gov , or by mail to the address on the fee coupon.
If mailing payment, laboratories must make the check payable to CLIA Laboratory Program and include the CLIA number on the memo portion of the check.

Section 6141 of the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1989, Public Law 101-239, requires laboratories participating in the Medicare program to comply with CLIA requirements. Therefore, virtually all laboratories in Texas must obtain a CLIA certificate to operate and be eligible for payment under Medicare and Medicaid.

CMS is now making CLIA certificates available online at no cost through the Quality, Certification and Oversight Reports (QCOR) Lookup Tool . Laboratories should be able to download all certificates generated after September 27, 2023, through QCOR . To access a certificate, a laboratory should choose "CLIA Laboratory Lookup" from the left menu bar.
How to Request a Revised or Replacement Certificate
Effective January 27, 2024, CMS implemented the following fees for obtaining revised or replacement CLIA certificates:
Replacement only; no changes to data (all certificate types): $75
Revised (facility name, laboratory director, or address) – based on certificate type Certificate of Waiver: $95
Certificate of Provider Performed Microscopy Procedures (PPMP): $150

HHSC CLIA will not generate replacement and revised certificates until the fee is paid. If a replacement certificate is needed, HHSC CLIA suggests checking the QCOR Lookup Tool to see if a certificate is available for download before requesting a paid replacement.
